curriculum.lesson_evidence: Anzac stands for Australian and New Zealand Army Corps. On 25 April 1915 Anzac soldiers landed at Gallipoli in Turkey. Anzac Day on 25 April now remembers all Australians and New Zealanders who have served and died in wars and conflicts. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people have also served. The day is for remembering, not for celebrating war.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
What does ANZAC stand for, and why is the main service held at dawn?

FEEDBACK
Australian and New Zealand Army Corps. Dawn services recall that the landing took place at dawn.

WATCH FOR
Believing Anzac Day celebrates winning a war misses that it honours those who served and those who died.
